text:
Maria Chen: @channel quick retro from today's Q4 spike — posting notes and asking for clarifying numbers. TL;DR: forecasting missed a marketing-driven burst, autoscaler thresholds + binpacking caused fragmentation, and we hit host-level memory pressure that looked like near-oom on several pools.

Alex Vasquez: thanks Maria. can you share the peak numbers?

Maria Chen: peak GPU utilization ~94% across us-west2-gpu-pool, sustained for ~18m. total GPU-hours consumed during the 6h event = 14,100h vs our forecasted 8,200h. burst was ~1.7x forecast.

Rajesh Narayan: that 1.7x matches the unexpected customer campaign + env test traffic. Product sent heads-up, but we didn't map it to model throughput.

Priya Sundar: we had a large rerank/embedding job from a single enterprise customer that spiked batch sizes; it amplified GPU memory usage.

Emily Park: observed queue backlog on the batch scheduler — throughput throttled because nodes were fragmented (lots of small pods with reserved memory). binpacking left ~20% unusable GPU memory.

Kevin Liao: oncall saw OOM killer traces on a few hosts; logs show GPU memory pressure then host-level swap thrashing. looked like NVLINK page faults in some drivers.

capacity-bot: Incident alert created: INC-2024-4471. Autoscaler actions: failed to add capacity due to quota check delay (AWS quota request pending).

Alex Vasquez: important: the autoscaler attempted scale up but was rate-limited by internal quota checks. we should separate quota validation from the critical path.

Maria Chen: agreed. also our headroom buffer of 15% was insufficient for Q4 surges and large single-customer batch jobs.

Rajesh Narayan: suggestion: change headroom policy to dynamic headroom = max(15%, p95-forecast * 0.25) for Q4 windows and known campaigns.

Priya Sundar: +1. also enforce smarter binpacking: prefer colocating small jobs onto same GPU when memory <= 32GB free to avoid fragmentation.

Emily Park: added a quick config snippet that helped in testing:
```json
{"autoscaler": {"min_nodes": 10, "scale_up_cooldown": 45, "concurrent_scale_ops": 2},
"binpack": {"strategy": "memory-first", "small_job_threshold_mb": 32768}}
```

Kevin Liao: ops notes: driver version on affected hosts was 545.57, we saw known NVLINK regression — patching to 545.73 reduced page fault rate in staging. schedule rolling driver update for us-west2.

Maria Chen: cost impact: incremental GPU-hours ~5,900h over forecast; estimated extra run cost ~$77k for the 6h event (on-demand equivalent). this needs to be flagged to finance for Q4 variance.

Rajesh Narayan: forecasting error root cause breakdown: 40% = untagged customer batch, 35% = marketing-driven user traffic, 25% = model config changes increasing memory per token.

Alex Vasquez: we should add an early warning pipeline: monitor queue growth + 5m derivative of GPU utilization + pending scale requests. threshold -> automated temporary throttle to non-critical low-tier customers.

Priya Sundar: propose: implement soft-throttle policy for background jobs and add per-customer burst caps for enterprise customers during high-demand windows.

Emily Park: i'll add dashboard tiles: 1) per-pool usable memory percentage, 2) fragmentation ratio, 3) pending_scale_requests. will also add a synthetic load test simulating large batch jobs.

Kevin Liao: immediate actions we performed this morning: 1) increased headroom on us-west2 by 30% (manual reserve), 2) restarted batch scheduler with memory-first binpack, 3) rolled back a recent model config change for one customer that doubled KV cache.

Maria Chen: long-term action items we agreed on in the call:
- (A) dynamic headroom during known campaign windows + automated calendar integration with product marketing.
- (B) decouple quota validation from autoscaler critical path; allow optimistic scale-up with async quota verification.
- (C) driver patch rollout plan for NVLINK regression (start next maintenance window).
- (D) enforce binpack memory-first strategy and add fragmentation metric to SLOs.
- (E) cost guardrail: auto-notify Finance + create temporary budget threshold to prevent surprise Q4 hits.

Priya Sundar: can we get owners? I can take (D) and (E).

Emily Park: i'll take (A) and add the dashboards.

Rajesh Narayan: i'll own (B) with Alex.

Kevin Liao: i'll coordinate (C) with eng-infra and schedule the patch.

Maria Chen: thanks everyone. i'll open a proper postmortem doc with timelines + shard-level logs and link it to INC-2024-4471. please drop any additional notes here. :thumbsup:

Alex Vasquez: note for retrospective — update forecasting model to ingest customer campaign calendar and create a simple multiplier for windows flagged "promo".

Emily Park: follow-up: will run a 2x synthetic against staging next week to validate new binpack logic.

capacity-bot: Reminder: add "postmortem-read" tag and set review meeting for 2024-11-07 16:00 UTC.

Maria Chen: last: thanks to oncall and infra for the quick manual headroom bump. saved a longer outage.

Kevin Liao: +1. small wins but big learning.

Priya Sundar: closing notes — prioritize burst caps for background/low-tier jobs first, then enterprise caps.

Maria Chen: end of thread; will paste postmortem link here once created.
